claims.claim: Exact harmonic duality gives a polynomial bound on fixed-width boundary signatures.
claims.evidence: For a finite transient binary graph with absorbing terminal set T, summation by parts gives x^-(t)-y^-(t)=Σ_v(d_y(v)-d_x(v))g_t(v) for every t∈T. Harmonicity gives g_t(v)=(h_t(s_1(v))-h_t(s_0(v)))/2, so |g_t(v)|≤1/2 and each terminal coordinate has diameter at most N/2. Conservation fixes the sum of terminal inflows; hence integral vectors number at most (floor(N/2)+1)^(|T|-1), polynomial for fixed |T|. The realization assertion is also sound: with φ≡1 and prescribed d∈[0,1]^N, writing edge flows as (t_v+d_v)/2 and (t_v-d_v)/2 yields an affine system whose nonterminal matrix has spectral radius below one. Iteration from t≡1 converges while retaining t_v≥1, proving nonnegativity. Choosing d_y-d_x=sign(g) realizes equality for two terminals.
claims.witness: For φ≡1, take d_y(v)=1,d_x(v)=0 when g(v)>0 and d_y(v)=0,d_x(v)=1 when g(v)<0; arbitrary equal choices work when g(v)=0. The resulting two realizable flows have terminal-inflow difference Σ_v|g(v)|.
claims.search_method: Independent algebraic derivation from harmonicity, flow conservation, transience, and integer-coordinate counting.

claims.claim: A general range bound survives at arbitrary level width, but it can grow linearly with the number of levels.
claims.evidence: An edge out of L_i cannot end below L_{i-1}, by the definition of distance to the sinks. A uniformly random walk starting at level at least i reaches L_{i-1} almost surely before absorption, so the strong Markov property puts its hitting probability in [m_{i-1},M_{i-1}]. Thus the level ranges are nested. Both successors of v∈L_i consequently lie in that interval in hitting-probability value, and harmonicity gives |g(v)|=|h(s_0(v))-h(s_1(v))|/2≤W_{i-1}/2. Summing over r vertices per positive level proves Σ_v|g(v)|≤(r/2)Σ_iW_{i-1}. Claim 2 supplies a family where the gap mass is Θ(k), so the asserted linear growth is genuinely attainable rather than merely slack in the upper bound.
claims.witness: The width-three family of claim 2 has gap mass k(k+7)/(4(k+1)), which is at least k/4 and hence grows linearly with its k positive levels.
claims.search_method: Independent proof from the distance inequality, almost-sure absorption, first-hitting decomposition, and harmonicity; cross-checked against the exact family in claim 2.

claims.claim: For width three, the gap mass and same-supply switching-flow diameter are unbounded; the width-two stability lemma fails already with two positive levels.
claims.evidence: The stated values satisfy every harmonic equation and are unique because the finite chain is transient. The absolute gaps sum to k(k+7)/(4(k+1)), which is at least k/4 and is therefore unbounded. The prescribed-imbalance construction from claim 0 realizes this entire gap mass as a same-φ sink-inflow difference. For k=2, the listed x and y are nonnegative, have even-minus-odd flow in {0,1}, and have net outflow one at every nonsink. Their sink-1 inflows are exactly 10/3 and 11/6, differing by 3/2>1. Padding preserves exact level widths and adds k(k+3)/(4(k+1)) gap mass per extra rail, giving the stated formula for every fixed r>3.
claims.witness: At k=2 and φ≡1, the explicit six-vertex flows in the draft satisfy all switching-flow constraints and produce sink-1 inflows 10/3 and 11/6. The parametric gap formula k(k+7)/(4(k+1)) proves unboundedness.
claims.search_method: Derived the harmonic values and gap sum symbolically, then ran an exact Fraction-based checker over k=2,…,100 and r=3,…,10; it also solved representative prescribed-imbalance systems exactly and checked the explicit k=2 certificate.

claims.claim: Within-level hitting-probability order is not locally determined at width three.
claims.evidence: Both completions are simple binary graphs with L_1={a,b,c}, L_2={X,Y,Z}, and every vertex reaches a sink. They have identical sinks and identical outgoing edges from L_1. Exact solution of their harmonic systems gives (h(a),h(b),h(c))=(3/22,1/22,1/2) in completion A and (1/22,3/22,1/2) in completion B. Thus the strict a-versus-b order reverses while all data available to the asserted local rule remains unchanged.
claims.witness: Completion A uses X→(c,b), Y→(a,b) and has h(a)>h(b); completion B uses X→(a,b), Y→(c,a) and has h(a)<h(b), while a→(0,X), b→(0,Y), and c→(0,1) are common.
claims.search_method: Constructed both graphs, verified their exact distance levels and simplicity, and solved both harmonic linear systems using rational Gaussian elimination.

target_evidence: The exact target asks whether ARRIVAL is polynomial-time solvable for every fixed r>2, beginning with r=3. The draft supplies neither a polynomial-time algorithm nor a contrary complexity classification, and its boundary-signature count applies only after the entire injection vector is fixed. It therefore does not fully resolve the target. It does, however, establish material correct progress: a polynomial fixed-supply boundary-total bound and explicit width-three counterexamples to both the constant flow-diameter estimate and the local hitting-order recursion used at width two. The final writeup expressly says the target remains unresolved and identifies varying supply vectors as the remaining obstacle. Accordingly, VALID_PARTIAL_PROGRESS is appropriate and the draft's claimed resolution of PARTIAL is ACCURATE.
